sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If you ever find yourself driving around the Midwest looking for a historic corn mill or a German culture festival or a chair factory,
sentences.zh: 如果你开车经过美国中西部，想找一座历史悠久的玉米磨坊、一场德国文化节或一家椅子工厂，

sentences.en: there's a chance you might end up in the small town of Jasper, Indiana.
sentences.zh: 你很有可能会来到印第安纳州的一个小镇——贾斯珀。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Driving through what looks to be more or less downtown Jasper, heading over to my first interview.
sentences.zh: 正开车穿过贾斯珀的市中心，前往我的第一次采访地点。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: That's reporter Jasper Davidoff reporting from Jasper, Indiana, which admittedly is a little confusing.
sentences.zh: 那是记者贾斯珀·达维多夫在印第安纳州的贾斯珀进行报道，这确实有点让人困惑。

sentences.en: And you're James?
sentences.zh: 你是詹姆斯？

sentences.en: Well, Jasper.
sentences.zh: 嗯，贾斯珀。

sentences.en: I was going to say, with a name like Jasper, you had to come to Jasper.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，名字叫贾斯珀，你就得来贾斯珀。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 我是说，很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: I was in Jasper, the place, this past fall because I wanted to talk with a guy named Jim Tin.
sentences.zh: 去年秋天我去了贾斯珀这个地方，因为我想采访一位叫吉姆·廷的人。

sentences.en: My name is Jim Tin with my wife, Pat.
sentences.zh: 我叫吉姆·廷，这是我妻子帕特。

sentences.en: Jasper is our home.
sentences.zh: 贾斯珀是我们的家。

sentences.en: I was born here.
sentences.zh: 我出生在这里。

sentences.en: Jim's dad, Herb Tin, was the mayor of Jasper back in the 1940s and 50s.
sentences.zh: 吉姆的父亲赫伯·廷在20世纪40年代和50年代曾担任贾斯珀的市长。

sentences.en: And when Jim was about seven years old, the town did something kind of radical.
sentences.zh: 当吉姆大约七岁时，这个小镇做了一件相当激进的事情。

sentences.en: Something that no other city had done before.
sentences.zh: 一件此前没有任何城市做过的事情。

sentences.en: They made garbage illegal.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布垃圾非法。

sentences.en: As of August 1st, 1950, they drew a bright line and said,
sentences.zh: 从1950年8月1日起，他们划下了一道明确的界线，并宣布：

sentences.en: if you were in the city, they would no longer collect any garbage.
sentences.zh: 如果你身处市内，他们将不再收集任何垃圾。

sentences.en: Although the city was still collecting stuff like plastics, soup cans, a lot of what you might recycle today,
sentences.zh: 尽管当时城市仍在收集塑料、汤罐头等今天可能回收的物品，

sentences.en: it was no longer picking up organic waste, or what the city called garbage.
sentences.zh: 但不再回收有机废物，或者说城市所定义的“垃圾”。

sentences.en: That's stuff like yard trimmings or the yucky things that people typically throw out,
sentences.zh: 那是指庭院修剪下来的残枝，或是人们通常扔掉的恶心东西，

sentences.en: like chicken bones, rotten fruit, eggshells.
sentences.zh: 比如鸡骨头、烂水果、蛋壳。

sentences.en: And this Sanitation Vanishing Act was made possible by a relatively new appliance,
sentences.zh: 而这场“垃圾消失术”之所以能实现，得益于一种相对较新的家电，

sentences.en: one that would soon make its way into kitchens across the country.
sentences.zh: 一种很快就会进入全国各地厨房的设备。

sentences.en: The Garbage Disposer.
sentences.zh: 食物垃圾处理器。

sentences.en: The Garbage Disposer is that little grinding machine at the bottom of a lot of kitchen sinks.
sentences.zh: 食物垃圾处理器就是安装在许多厨房水槽底部的小型研磨机。

sentences.en: Most people call it the Disposal with an AL, or the Insinkerator, or even the Garburator.
sentences.zh: 大多数人称之为“Disposal”，或者“Insinkerator”（爱适易），甚至“Garburator”。

sentences.en: But to keep things simple and avoid brand names, we're going to use the generic Disposer with an ER.
sentences.zh: 但为了简单起见并避免品牌名称，我们将使用通用的“Disposer”一词。

sentences.en: I know it sounds a little weird.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来有点奇怪。

sentences.en: If you live in the United States, you either have a garbage disposer in your sink,
sentences.zh: 如果你住在美国，你的水槽里要么装有一个食物垃圾处理器，

sentences.en: or you at least have a friend or relative with one in theirs.
sentences.zh: 要么你至少有朋友或亲戚的家里装有一个。

sentences.en: According to the 2013 American Housing Survey, nearly half of all households have a disposer.
sentences.zh: 根据2013年美国住房调查，近一半的家庭拥有这种处理器。

sentences.en: In other countries, these machines aren't nearly as common.
sentences.zh: 在其他国家，这些机器并不那么普遍。

sentences.en: And until recently, the most I ever really thought about a disposer was as a kid,
sentences.zh: 直到最近，我对处理器的全部印象还停留在小时候，

sentences.en: when my mom got mad at me for throwing cherry pits down ours.
sentences.zh: 那时我妈因为我把樱桃核扔进处理器里而对我大发雷霆。

sentences.en: But over the last couple months, I've become a little obsessed with the monster under our sinks.
sentences.zh: 但在过去几个月里，我开始对水槽下的这个“怪物”有点着迷了。

sentences.en: And how despite the awful sounds it makes,
sentences.zh: 尽管它发出的声音很可怕，

sentences.en: the disposer quietly managed to become a staple of the American kitchen,
sentences.zh: 但处理器还是悄然成为了美式厨房的标配，

sentences.en: and changed the way we think about our food waste.
sentences.zh: 并改变了我们看待食物垃圾的方式。

sentences.en: The story of the garbage disposer starts long before Jasper, Indiana's experiment.
sentences.zh: 食物垃圾处理器的故事早在印第安纳州贾斯珀的实验之前就开始了。

sentences.en: It even starts, you could say, before the invention of garbage.
sentences.zh: 甚至可以说，是在“垃圾”这个概念被发明之前就开始了。

sentences.en: It used to be that people didn't have much garbage.
sentences.zh: 过去，人们并没有多少垃圾。

sentences.en: They didn't create much garbage.
sentences.zh: 他们制造的垃圾很少。

sentences.en: If something broke, you would take it back to the person who made it to get it fixed.
sentences.zh: 如果东西坏了，你会把它带回制造者那里去修理。

sentences.en: Or there would be people who specialized in repairs who would fix things.
sentences.zh: 或者会有专门从事维修的人来修理东西。

sentences.en: Susan Strasser is a historian who studies consumerism, domesticity, and, yes, garbage.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·斯特拉瑟是一位研究消费主义、家庭生活以及——没错——垃圾的历史学家。

sentences.en: She says that up until the late 1800s, people were just much less wasteful.
sentences.zh: 她说，直到19世纪末，人们浪费的情况要少得多。

sentences.en: People ate food scraps.
sentences.zh: 人们会吃掉食物残渣。

sentences.en: If you read books about how to run your household,
sentences.zh: 如果你读过关于如何操持家务的书，

sentences.en: people are advised to, when they clear the table, save food.
sentences.zh: 书中会建议人们在清理餐桌时，要节省食物。

sentences.en: And the expectation was that good food would be eaten by people.
sentences.zh: 而且人们普遍认为好的食物应该被吃掉。

sentences.en: Food scraps weren't thought of as a burden, but as an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 食物残渣不被视为负担，而是一种机会。

sentences.en: A way to save for another meal, or to repurpose into candles and soap.
sentences.zh: 一种为下一顿饭节省开支，或将其改造成蜡烛和肥皂的方法。

sentences.en: The idea of wasting food was really anathema to most people.
sentences.zh: 浪费食物的想法对大多数人来说简直是深恶痛绝的。

sentences.en: Food that wasn't quite good enough for the people could be fed to animals.
sentences.zh: 不太适合人类食用的食物可以喂给动物。

sentences.en: There were pets, dogs, and cats.
sentences.zh: 当时人们养宠物，比如狗和猫。

sentences.en: But also, many, many people kept chickens, even in urban and suburban areas.
sentences.zh: 而且，许多人还养鸡，即使是在城市和郊区也是如此。

sentences.en: And chickens will eat pretty much anything and give you eggs in return.
sentences.zh: 鸡几乎什么都吃，作为回报，它们会为你提供鸡蛋。

sentences.en: But at the turn of the century, the commercialization of food made more of it available at a cheaper price.
sentences.zh: 但在世纪之交，食品的商业化使得更多食物以更便宜的价格供应。

sentences.en: And that abundance made it easier for people to throw out their scraps.
sentences.zh: 这种充裕让人们更容易扔掉残羹剩饭。

sentences.en: Around the same time, lots of people were moving from the countryside into U.S.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，许多人从乡村搬到了美国城市。

sentences.en: cities.
sentences.zh: 所有的食物垃圾实际上都堆积在街上，不仅造成了臭气熏天的问题，还引发了公共卫生问题。

sentences.en: And all that food waste was literally piling up on the street, creating not only a smelly problem, but a public health one.
sentences.zh: 那时，许多人仍然相信霍乱等疾病是通过恶臭传播的，

sentences.en: Back then, many still believed that diseases like cholera were spreading through noxious odors,
sentences.zh: 包括那些从垃圾堆中散发出来的臭味。

sentences.en: including those emanating from piles of garbage.
sentences.zh: “垃圾”（Garbage）在当时是一个相当专业术语，确实是指易腐烂的废物，

sentences.en: Garbage being a pretty technical term at the time that really did refer to perishable waste
sentences.zh: 而不是指那些可能不太容易腐烂、被扔掉的“废弃物”（Rubbish）。

sentences.en: as opposed to rubbish that might have been less perishable products that were being thrown away.
sentences.zh: 安娜·泽塔是弗吉尼亚理工大学的食品历史学家。

sentences.en: Anna Zeta is a food historian at Virginia Tech.
sentences.zh: 她说，与今天“垃圾”这个包罗万象的定义不同，

sentences.en: She says that, unlike the catch-all definition garbage has today,
sentences.zh: 它过去专门指有机废物。

sentences.en: it used to refer specifically to organic waste.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没听出来的话，这就是我在接下来的故事中继续使用“垃圾”一词的方式。

sentences.en: Which, in case you haven't already caught on, is how I'm going to keep using garbage for the rest of this story.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，联邦和州政府并没有多大意愿去解决日益严重的垃圾问题。

sentences.en: Around the country, there wasn't much of an appetite by federal and state governments
sentences.zh: 相反，垃圾收集的工作落在了各个城市和城镇身上。

sentences.en: to take on the growing garbage problem.
sentences.zh: 因此，市政法规开始以相当零散的方式制定，

sentences.en: Instead, the job of waste collection fell to individual cities and towns.
sentences.zh: 在不同地区非常碎片化，试图解决这些垃圾带来的问题。

sentences.en: And so municipal regulations began to be developed in quite scattershot ways,
sentences.zh: 一些城市开始提供收集服务，将垃圾运往垃圾场。

sentences.en: very piecemeal in different localities, to try to address what was happening with this garbage.
sentences.zh: 另一些城市则要求市民将厨房垃圾与其他废物分开。

sentences.en: Some municipalities started collection services to haul their waste to a dump.
sentences.zh: 丢弃的食物会被送到当地农民那里，作为猪饲料。

sentences.en: Others demanded citizens split up their kitchen refuse from their other waste.
sentences.zh: 但那里也出现了许多健康问题，因为许多所谓的“未煮熟的垃圾”

sentences.en: The discarded food would get sent to local farmers who used it as feed for their hogs.
sentences.zh: 可能携带各种病原体，导致猪群中广泛爆发疾病，

sentences.en: But there, too, a lot of problems for health emerged in that a lot of so-called uncooked garbage
sentences.zh: 人们担心其中一些病原体会传染给食用这些猪肉的人类。

sentences.en: could carry various kinds of pathogens that caused widespread disease in the pigs themselves,
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪20年代初，这些杂乱无章的垃圾收集系统

sentences.en: some of which was feared would carry over into any humans who were eating the meat that came from the pigs.
sentences.zh: 已经难以跟上20世纪消费主义的步伐。

sentences.en: By the early 1920s, these haphazard systems of garbage collection
sentences.zh: 城镇在焚烧垃圾，甚至将其倾倒在当地河流中。

sentences.en: were struggling to keep up with 20th century consumerism.
sentences.zh: 于是，通用电气公司的工程师们介入了这场垃圾漩涡。

sentences.en: Cities and towns were burning garbage, even throwing it in their local river.
sentences.zh: 一些社区已经开始用大型机器研磨垃圾，

sentences.en: And so into this maelstrom of detritus stepped the engineers at the General Electric Company.
sentences.zh: 并将其冲入当地的下水道。

sentences.en: A few communities had started grinding up their garbage in these massive machines
sentences.zh: 通用电气采用了这个全新的概念——将污水与食物垃圾混合——并试图将其推广。

sentences.en: and washing it down into their local sewers.
sentences.zh: 如果你能用大型研磨机处理城镇的垃圾，

sentences.en: GE took this totally new concept, mixing sewage with food waste, and tried to expand on it.
sentences.zh: 那么能不能制造小型家用研磨机，从源头上消除垃圾呢？

sentences.en: If you could use a large-scale grinder to get rid of the town's garbage,
sentences.zh: 因此，1930年，两名通用电气代表前往纽约州斯克内克塔迪，

sentences.en: could you build small household ones to eliminate garbage at the source?
sentences.zh: 拜访了一位名叫莫里斯·科恩的卫生工程师。

sentences.en: So in 1930, two GE representatives traveled to Schenectady, New York,
sentences.zh: 他同意帮助通用电气进行研究，甚至开始在自己家中进行实验，

sentences.en: to visit a sanitary engineer named Morris Cohn.
sentences.zh: 用绞肉机粉碎食物，然后把残渣冲进马桶。

sentences.en: He agreed to help GE conduct their research and even started experimenting in his own home,
sentences.zh: 没过多久，所有的冲洗都取得了成果。

sentences.en: pulverizing food in a meat grinder and flushing the results down the toilet.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“处理器”（Disposal）。

sentences.en: And before long, all that flushing yielded a result.
sentences.zh: 这就是玉米芯等粗颗粒在通用电气处理器内部的处理过程。

sentences.en: They called it the disposal.
sentences.zh: 几乎在还没来得及向你介绍完的时间里，

sentences.en: And here's how coarse particles like corn cobs get the works inside a General Electric Disposal.
sentences.zh: 它们就会被研磨成玉米粒大小或更小，

sentences.en: In almost less time than it takes to tell you about it,
sentences.zh: 并被送入下水道一去不复返。

sentences.en: they'll be whittled down to corn kernel size or smaller
sentences.zh: 到了30年代末，人们开始对食物垃圾处理器感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: and given a one-way ticket down the drain.
sentences.zh: 《科学美国人》预测，处理器将使垃圾桶成为历史。

sentences.en: By the late 30s, people started getting very excited about garbage disposers.
sentences.zh: 《家居与花园》杂志的一篇文章向读者介绍了新的垃圾处理技术，

sentences.en: Scientific American predicted that the disposer would make the garbage can obsolete.
sentences.zh: 比如橡胶刮板和打蜡的垃圾桶内衬。

sentences.en: An article in House and Garden magazine introduced readers to new garbage tech
sentences.zh: 但它给予最高评价的还是处理器。

sentences.en: like rubber plate scrapers and waxed garbage pail liners.
sentences.zh: 你不会再有老鼠了。

sentences.en: But its highest praise was for the disposer.
sentences.zh: 你的厨房里不会再有臭味了。

sentences.en: You're not going to have rats.
sentences.zh: 你再也不会有食物垃圾带来的问题了，

sentences.en: You're not going to have the smelly stuff in your kitchen.
sentences.zh: 因为你直接把它们冲进下水道就行了。

sentences.en: You're not going to have the problems that come with food waste anymore
sentences.zh: 尽管有这些炒作，通用电气等公司仍然没有得到他们真正想要的东西：

sentences.en: because you're going to wash it down the drain.
sentences.zh: 一个测试点，一个能证明处理器不仅对单个家庭有益，

sentences.en: Even with all this hype, companies like GE still didn't have what they really wanted,
sentences.zh: 而且对整个社区都有切实改善的地方。

sentences.en: a test site, a place to prove that the disposer wasn't just a benefit for an individual household,
sentences.zh: 贾斯珀很快就会改变这一切。

sentences.en: but a bona fide improvement for an entire community.
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.zh: 抱歉，我不是在说你。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 我是这个意思。

sentences.en: Sorry, I wasn't talking about you.
sentences.zh: 印第安纳州的贾斯珀很快就会改变这一切。

sentences.en: Here's what I meant.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是个有独创性的人。

sentences.en: Jasper, Indiana, would soon change all that.
sentences.zh: 他很有创造力，善于解决问题，而且非常有健康意识，非常有公民意识。

sentences.en: Dad was an original thinker.
sentences.zh: 那是吉姆·廷再次发言。

sentences.en: He was a creative person and a good problem solver, and he was very health-conscious, very civic-minded.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲在40和50年代担任贾斯珀市长。

sentences.en: That's Jim Tinn again.
sentences.zh: 当时，贾斯珀正面临着大量的公共卫生问题。

sentences.en: His dad was the mayor of Jasper back in the 40s and 50s.
sentences.zh: 老鼠和苍蝇是镇上的常见困扰。

sentences.en: At the time, Jasper was struggling with a ton of public health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 1947年爆发了猪霍乱，追溯起来是因为农民用垃圾喂猪。

sentences.en: Rats and flies were a common nuisance in town.
sentences.zh: 紧接着是脊髓灰质炎疫情，当时，

sentences.en: There was an outbreak of swine cholera in 1947, which traced back to the garbage farmers had fed the pigs.
sentences.zh: 当地人认为这可能与在露天垃圾槽周围嗡嗡作响的苍蝇有关。

sentences.en: And this was followed quickly by the polio epidemic, which, at the time,
sentences.zh: 所以有一天，廷市长和妻子在附近的埃文斯维尔散步时，

sentences.en: locals felt might be related to the flies buzzing around open troughs of garbage.
sentences.zh: 偶然发现了解决镇上问题的办法。

sentences.zh: 他在西尔斯百货的展示橱窗里看到了一个处理器。

sentences.en: when he stumbled on a solution to the town's probleMs.
sentences.zh: 橱窗里的标语写着：

sentences.zh: 告别你的垃圾桶。

sentences.en: The sign in the window read,
sentences.zh: 那一刻，廷市长看到了改变一切的机会。

sentences.en: Say goodbye to your garbage can.
sentences.zh: 一周后，市长买了他自己的食物垃圾处理器。

sentences.en: And in that moment, Mayor Tinn saw an opportunity to change everything.
sentences.zh: 这台设备加上安装费花了他大约125美元，相当于今天的1500美元左右。

sentences.en: A week later, the mayor bought his very own garbage disposer.
sentences.zh: 就像之前那些技术精湛、老练的卫生工程师一样，

sentences.zh: 市长开始把各种东西扔进处理器里测试结果。

sentences.en: And like the highly technical, sophisticated, sanitary engineers that came before him,
sentences.zh: 我们家里装了一个处理器，我相信是在48年。

sentences.en: the mayor just started chucking things down his disposer to test the results.
sentences.zh: 父亲觉得我们必须带头示范，

sentences.en: We put a disposal in our house, I believe it was in 48.
